title: PD-MT241-NativeBlockDiffEngine

scope.summary:
GOAL: Implement the block-level native prose diff + three-way prose merge that WP-KERNEL-012 MT-009 DEFERRED. The MT-009 header (src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/diff_engine.rs lines ~5-19, verified 2026-07-21) states the block-level prose diff over the native rich-document format was deferred because that format 'DOES NOT EXIST yet'; it left [`diff_json_blocks`] (lines ~496-526) as an unwired SEAM doing a naive index-only alignment. That format now EXISTS: the typed block tree in src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/document_model/ (NodeKind = Doc, Paragraph, Heading(1..3), Blockquote, CodeBlock, OrderedList, BulletList, ListItem, Table, TableRow, TableCell, TableHeader, TaskItem, HardBreak, HorizontalRule; inline atoms via Child::{Block, Text(TextLeaf), HsLink(HsLinkNode), Transclusion(TransclusionNode)}; BlockNode{kind, attrs: HashMap<String,serde_json::Value>, children: Vec<Child>}). This MT ports the React reference app/src/lib/editor/document_diff_merge.ts EXACTLY (it is the parity target and is DELETED afterward by the TR family MT-261..264; parity fixtures must be authored while it still exists — see MT-245), then hardens it with stable-block-id matching + a content-similarity fallback for moved/edited blocks. Pure-function core, NO UI (UI is MT-242/243/244).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) NEW module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/document_model/prose_diff.rs holding the typed BlockDiff + BlockMergePlan types and the pure engine; (b) one `pub mod prose_diff;` line + re-exports added to src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/document_model/mod.rs; (c) REWIRE the deferred seam in code_editor/diff_engine.rs: `diff_json_blocks(&[serde_json::Value], &[serde_json::Value])` stops doing the placeholder index alignment and delegates to the new LCS/identity block aligner (keeping its existing `Vec<DiffBlock>` signature and the existing `json_block_diff_classifies_by_index` test still passing on non-moved inputs, or updating that test in-place to the LCS behaviour with a comment); (d) unit tests. NO egui, NO tokio, NO backend, NO route calls.

DETAILED SPEC — the parity rule set ported from document_diff_merge.ts (enumerated after reading the whole file 2026-07-21):

BLOCK EXTRACTION: documentBlocks(doc) = doc.content array when present else []. Native equivalent: the ordered top-level `Child::Block` children of a `RichDocument`/doc `BlockNode` (a document is a flat list of top-level blocks; nested block children stay INSIDE their block node and are compared as part of that node's value).

DIFF (buildRichDocumentDiff): align leftBlocks vs rightBlocks by `longestCommonBlockSubsequence` — a classic LCS DP over block EQUALITY (jsonDeepEquals in TS; native: structural BlockNode PartialEq, which the model already derives). Walk the LCS matches; between consecutive matches, `alignGap` pairs the first min(leftGap,rightGap) unmatched blocks positionally (these become `modified`/`unchanged` pairs) and emits the leftover left blocks as left-only, leftover right blocks as right-only. For each aligned pair build a BlockDiff:
  - leftNode == None  -> status `Added` (React `added`).
  - rightNode == None -> status `Removed` (React `removed`).
  - both present and equal -> status `Unchanged` (React `unchanged`; native enum name `Unchanged`, aliased to code_editor DiffStatus::Equal at the boundary).
  - both present and unequal -> status `Modified`.
  Each BlockDiff carries: block_index (position in the aligned sequence), status, kind (Prose | Code | Unknown per diffKind: Code if either side isCodeBlock i.e. NodeKind::CodeBlock / Tiptap type 'monacoCodeBlock' on the JSON path, Prose if either side is any other typed block, else Unknown), left_node/right_node (Option clones), and left_text/right_text (nodeText: recursive plain-text extraction — a text leaf's text, a code block's code, else the concatenation of children's text; matches TS nodeText).

MODIFIED-BLOCK INTRA-BLOCK TEXT DIFF: for a `Modified` pair, additionally compute an inline text diff of left_text vs right_text using the `similar` crate (already a workspace dep, used by code_editor/diff_engine.rs), exposed as an Option<Vec<InlineTextSpan>> where InlineTextSpan{ tag: Equal|Insert|Delete, text: String } (from similar::TextDiff::from_words or from_chars — use words to match how a reader perceives prose edits; document the choice). This is the native ENHANCEMENT the React file lacks; it must NOT change block-level status classification.

STABLE-ID + SIMILARITY HARDENING (native superset, must be parity-neutral on the MT-245 fixtures): before falling back to pure LCS-by-equality, match blocks by a stable id when present — read `attrs.get("id")` or `attrs.get("blockId")` (BlockNode has no dedicated id field; ids ride in the free-form `attrs` map). Two blocks with the same non-empty stable id are treated as the SAME block (a `Modified` if their content differs, `Unchanged` if equal) even if they moved. For blocks WITHOUT ids, after LCS, run a content-similarity pass (similar::TextDiff ratio over nodeText) to pair a leftover left-only block with a leftover right-only block when their similarity ratio exceeds a threshold (default 0.5, `PROSE_DIFF_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` const) — turning a false Added+Removed pair into one Modified for a heavily edited or moved block. GUARANTEE: on inputs where no block carries an id and no cross-gap move exists (the parity-fixture shape MT-245 authors), this hardening is inert and the output equals the pure TS LCS result. Document this invariant in the module docs.

3-WAY MERGE (planRichDocumentMerge): count = max(base,local,remote block counts). For each index 0..count: baseNode/localNode/remoteNode = that index's block on each side (None past the end). localChanged = base != local; remoteChanged = base != remote. If NOT localChanged AND NOT remoteChanged -> emit NO block (React `continue`). Else classify BlockMergeStatus:
  - localChanged && remoteChanged -> (local == remote) ? `BothSame` : `Conflict`.
  - localChanged only -> `LocalOnly`.
  - remoteChanged only -> `RemoteOnly`.
  Each BlockMergeBlock carries: block_index, status, base_node/local_node/remote_node (Option clones), local_text/remote_text (nodeText). NOTE THE ASYMMETRY (verified in the TS): the DIFF path uses LCS alignment, but the MERGE path uses positional INDEX alignment (max length, per-index compare) — port both exactly as written; do NOT LCS-align the merge.

APPLY (applyRichDocumentMergePlan): max = max(base,local,remote counts). Build a by-index map of the plan blocks. For each index 0..max: if a plan block exists, selected = selectedMergeNode(block, choices): `LocalOnly`/`BothSame` -> local_node; `RemoteOnly` -> remote_node; `Conflict` -> the operator/agent choice for that index (Local->local_node, Remote->remote_node, Both->[local_node, remote_node]); an UNRESOLVED conflict is a typed error (React throws). If no plan block exists at an index, selected = local_node else remote_node (the React `?? `). Flatten array selections. Return a merged block list (native: Vec<BlockNode>); the caller re-wraps it into a doc (React returns `{...local, content: merged}` — native preserves the local doc envelope and swaps its top-level block children).

ENGINE SHAPE: mirror code_editor/diff_engine.rs conventions — a stateless `ProseDiffEngine` with `diff(left:&RichDocument, right:&RichDocument) -> ProseDiff` and a `BlockMergeEngine` with `three_way(base,local,remote) -> BlockMergePlan` + `apply(plan, choices) -> Result<Vec<BlockNode>, ProseMergeError>`. Reuse `MergeChoice{Local,Remote,Both}` from code_editor::diff_engine (re-export, do not fork). Typed errors: `ProseMergeError::UnresolvedConflict{block_index}`.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read app/src/lib/editor/document_diff_merge.ts IN FULL (the parity target; RichDocumentDiffBlock status unchanged|modified|added|removed ~lines 10-23; RichDocumentMergePlan local_only|remote_only|both_same|conflict ~lines 29-49) and code_editor/diff_engine.rs (DiffStatus/DiffBlock/MergeStatus/MergeChoice/MergeBlock, and the deferred diff_json_blocks seam + its module header) before writing any code.
2. Read rich_editor/document_model/node.rs (BlockNode/Child/NodeKind/TextLeaf — note there is NO id field; attrs is the free-form id carrier) and doc_json.rs (RichDocument envelope, block_to_json, to_content_json_value, RICH_DOCUMENT_SCHEMA_VERSION) so the JSON<->typed boundary reuses the existing serializers.
3. Create prose_diff.rs with the BlockDiff/ProseDiff/BlockMergeBlock/BlockMergePlan/InlineTextSpan types + ProseDiffStatus{Unchanged,Added,Removed,Modified} + BlockMergeStatus{LocalOnly,RemoteOnly,BothSame,Conflict} + ProseMergeError. Implement LCS alignment (DP identical in shape to longestCommonBlockSubsequence), gap alignment (identical to alignGap), diffKind/nodeText, the stable-id + similarity hardening, the intra-block similar text diff, the index-aligned three_way, and apply.
4. Rewire code_editor/diff_engine.rs::diff_json_blocks to delegate to the new aligner (serialize each Value pair to the classification the LCS aligner produces, returning the same Vec<DiffBlock> with block-INDEX ranges); keep or update-in-place the json_block_diff_classifies_by_index test with a comment noting the LCS upgrade.
5. Add `pub mod prose_diff;` and re-exports to document_model/mod.rs.
6. Unit tests (see expected_tests): every status, the LCS move case, stable-id match across a move, similarity fallback turning Added+Removed into Modified, the merge classifications, both_same vs conflict, apply with each MergeChoice, unresolved-conflict typed error, and a battery of small fixtures whose classifications are asserted IDENTICAL to hand-computed document_diff_merge.ts output (the seed of the MT-245 parity corpus).
7. cargo build + clippy clean; run the tests.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (legacy React reference ONLY; the parity target document_diff_merge.ts is read, never edited here — its removal is TR MT-261..264)
acceptance_criteria: prose_diff.rs exists with ProseDiffEngine::diff over document_model RichDocument/BlockNode producing BlockDiff{block_index, status(Unchanged|Added|Removed|Modified), kind(Prose|Code|Unknown), left_node, right_node, left_text, right_text} via LCS block alignment.
Block alignment uses LCS over structural block equality with gap pairing that reproduces document_diff_merge.ts alignDiffBlocks/longestCommonBlockSubsequence classifications on parity fixtures.
A Modified block carries an intra-block inline text diff (Vec<InlineTextSpan> tagged Equal/Insert/Delete) computed via the similar crate; the inline diff never alters the block-level status.

Stable-id matching keys off attrs['id']/attrs['blockId'] (BlockNode has no id field) and treats same-id blocks as the same block across moves; the similarity fallback (default threshold 0.5, PROSE_DIFF_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD) fuses a leftover Added+Removed into one Modified for a moved/heavily-edited block.
The hardening is parity-neutral: on id-free, no-move inputs the diff output equals the pure LCS/TS result (asserted by a fixture test).

BlockMergeEngine::three_way ports planRichDocumentMerge EXACTLY: max-length INDEX alignment (not LCS), per-index localChanged/remoteChanged, no block emitted when neither side changed, BothSame vs Conflict when both changed, LocalOnly/RemoteOnly otherwise.

BlockMergeEngine::apply ports applyRichDocumentMergePlan: selectedMergeNode rules for each status, Both -> local then remote, missing-plan-index falls back to local else remote, and an unresolved Conflict returns ProseMergeError::UnresolvedConflict (React throws) rather than silently dropping a side.
MergeChoice{Local,Remote,Both} is re-exported from code_editor::diff_engine, not re-defined.

The deferred code_editor/diff_engine.rs::diff_json_blocks seam is rewired to delegate to the LCS/identity aligner (no longer the placeholder index-only alignment) and keeps its Vec<DiffBlock> signature.
The core is pure: no egui, no tokio, no backend/api/storage import (grep-provable); cargo build -p handshake-native and clippy -D warnings pass.
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake-native prose_block_diff -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'
implementation_notes: Verified grounding 2026-07-21 (wtc-native-editors-v1): code_editor/diff_engine.rs header lines ~5-19 declare the block-level prose diff DEFERRED and diff_json_blocks (lines ~496-526) a placeholder index-only alignment 'intentionally a simple index alignment (not the React LCS block alignment) because the native rich-document format is not yet defined; when E2 lands, this is the hook to replace with the format-aware alignment ported from buildRichDocumentDiff'. This MT is that replacement.

document_diff_merge.ts is the PARITY TARGET and will be DELETED by TR MT-261..264. All classification behaviour must be locked by fixtures in THIS MT (seed corpus) and the full parity suite in MT-245 WHILE the TS file still exists. Do not defer parity capture.

BlockNode has NO id field; stable ids live in the free-form attrs map (attrs['id'] / attrs['blockId']). Do not add an id field to BlockNode in this MT (that is a model change outside prose-diff scope); read ids out of attrs.

The DIFF uses LCS alignment; the MERGE uses positional index alignment. This asymmetry is faithful to the TS reference — do not 'fix' it by aligning the merge with LCS; MT-243's UI and MT-245's parity both assume the TS behaviour.

similar is already a workspace dependency (code_editor/diff_engine.rs uses TextDiff::from_lines). Reuse it for both the intra-block inline diff and the similarity-ratio fallback; do not add a new diff crate.

Reuse code_editor::diff_engine::{MergeChoice} and align the native ProseDiffStatus to DiffStatus at the code_editor boundary (Unchanged<->Equal) so MT-242's renderer can share one status vocabulary across code and prose diffs.

Cross-family seams (reference only, not authored here): MT-242 prose diff UI consumes ProseDiff; MT-243 prose merge UI consumes BlockMergePlan/apply; MT-244 annotations target contiguous changed-block runs; MT-245 parity+perf proofs BLOCK the TR MT-261 removal gate.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Pure-function diff/merge core over the typed document model; the operator-facing prose diff surface is MT-242, the merge UI is MT-243.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal engine MT with no operator-visible behaviour on its own; the UserManual entries land with the MT-242 prose diff view and MT-243 merge UI.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FlightRecorder: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — pure synchronous diff/merge functions emit no runtime events; diff/merge lifecycle events (if any) belong to the MT-242/243 UI surfaces.

internal_diagnostics: WIRED — alignment decisions (LCS match vs gap pairing vs stable-id match vs similarity-fallback fuse) and unresolved-conflict errors are typed/inspectable, not stringly, so a no-context model can trace why a block classified as it did.
Palmistry: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — no long-running process or child; synchronous pure functions.
risk_if_missed: The MT-009 deferred prose diff stays unwired: worktree-merge and notes conflict review keep falling back to line-level text diff over serialized JSON (noisy, block-blind) or the legacy React document_diff_merge.ts that TR MT-261..264 is about to delete, leaving the native editor with NO block-aware prose diff or 3-way merge and no parity anchor before the reference is removed.

risks: RISK-1: The native block diff SILENTLY diverges from document_diff_merge.ts (different alignment, different modified/added split), so once TR MT-261..264 deletes the TS reference there is no way to detect the regression and operators see wrong prose diffs.

RISK-2: The stable-id + similarity hardening changes classifications the TS never produced, breaking parity: a moved block that the TS reported as Removed+Added is fused into Modified and the parity fixtures disagree.
RISK-3: The three-way merge is wrongly LCS-aligned (copying the diff path) instead of index-aligned, producing different conflict sets than planRichDocumentMerge and silently mis-merging documents.
RISK-4: An unresolved conflict is silently resolved to one side (or drops a side) instead of erroring, so a merge 'succeeds' while discarding operator or agent edits.

RISK-5: nodeText / diffKind mis-handle code blocks (monacoCodeBlock / NodeKind::CodeBlock) or inline atoms (hsLink, loomTransclusion), so code-block and wikilink edits are misclassified or their text is lost from the diff.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Fixture tests assert native classifications equal hand-computed document_diff_merge.ts output; MT-245 promotes these into the full parity suite that BLOCKS the TR MT-261 removal gate.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): A parity-neutrality invariant test proves that on id-free, no-move inputs the hardened diff equals the pure LCS/TS result; the hardening only refines cases the TS could not express, never the fixtures.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): three_way is implemented as a max-length per-index compare with a dedicated test on inputs where LCS alignment WOULD give a different answer, asserting the index-aligned (TS) result.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): apply returns ProseMergeError::UnresolvedConflict for a Conflict with no choice; a negative test asserts the error and that no side is dropped; Both preserves local-then-remote order.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): nodeText/diffKind tests cover a code block (Code kind, code text extracted), an hsLink atom, and a loomTransclusion atom, asserting no text is lost and kind is correct.

research_provenance.source: Direct source inspection 2026-07-21 of wtc-native-editors-v1: code_editor/diff_engine.rs (deferred-prose-diff header lines ~5-19, diff_json_blocks seam lines ~496-526, DiffStatus/DiffBlock/MergeStatus{LocalOnly,RemoteOnly,BothSame,Conflict}/MergeChoice/MergeBlock, similar crate usage); rich_editor/document_model/node.rs (NodeKind full variant set, Child::{Block,Text,HsLink,Transclusion}, BlockNode{kind,attrs,children} with NO id field) and doc_json.rs (RichDocument envelope, block_to_json/to_content_json_value, RICH_DOCUMENT_SCHEMA_VERSION rich_document_v1). PARITY TARGET read in full: app/src/lib/editor/document_diff_merge.ts (RichDocumentDiffBlock status unchanged|modified|added|removed lines ~10-23; buildRichDocumentDiff -> alignDiffBlocks -> longestCommonBlockSubsequence + alignGap; diffStatus/diffKind/nodeText; RichDocumentMergePlan local_only|remote_only|both_same|conflict lines ~29-49; planRichDocumentMerge max-length index alignment + continue-when-unchanged; applyRichDocumentMergePlan + selectedMergeNode throw-on-unresolved).
corrections: The native rich-document format that MT-009 said 'DOES NOT EXIST yet' now EXISTS as rich_editor/document_model (delivered under WP-KERNEL-012 E2); this MT is the sanctioned replacement of the deferred diff_json_blocks seam, not new speculative work.

document_diff_merge.ts uses LCS for the DIFF but positional index alignment for the MERGE; both are ported verbatim. The stable-id + similarity matching is a native superset explicitly constrained to be parity-neutral on the MT-245 fixture corpus so it cannot invalidate the parity gate.
